reason: The cited evidence shows that grain boundary diffusion and precipitation occur in some multi-element alloys (E3, E4) and that one type of nanoparticle remains largely single-phase after annealing (E1), but no evidence supports the claims that segregation/precipitation improve stability or catalytic performance, nor that these mechanisms operate in the specific nanoparticle system proposed.
premises: Thermally-activated diffusion and segregation of elements to grain boundaries occurs in near-equiatomic multi-element nanoparticles
This segregation leads to precipitation of stable phases
The formation of these stable phases improves structural and chemical stability
The formation of these stable phases enhances catalytic activity and selectivity
These processes occur under annealing at 773-1173 K in inert atmosphere
